cells.tense: Right now faith shows up as behavior, carried in the body and spent only where it is due.
cells.act: care for it with fresh hands and see what it needs
cells.ask: Pick an open thing you keep holding shut. Give it a week of plain hands-on tending, noticing what it asks for before you change anything.
cells.core:
You keep what you have sworn to and you know what releasing costs, because you have paid it. So the load you put down does not come back. When something is finished, you can let it be finished, and people around an ending feel steadier for it, not abandoned. That is faith wearing work clothes. Nothing here has been decided yet, and that is not a problem to solve.
Feed that. Choose an open possibility you have been carrying — an arrangement, a plan, a responsibility close to finishing — and give it a week of small attention. Handle it at ordinary size, notice what it actually needs, and stop there. No decision is required to do this. The attention itself shows you whether it is alive, and the shape of it stays yours to choose. What opens can go on opening.
cells.sheetLine: You let go clean because you carried it full.
cells.verb: releasing, once it is complete, with the full weight of having borne it
cells.place: the open room before the choice, where anything can still become

cells.tense: Something not yet chosen is already being guarded against, and the bracing has moved ahead of the thing itself.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Write the situation you keep rehearsing on one page as it stands, no feeling words, nothing added — then follow what is written and close the notebook.
cells.core:
Nothing has been chosen yet, and the merits are already being weighed somewhere behind the eyes — exits mapped, arguments finished, most of the work spent on a decision no one has been asked to make. Readiness that fast gets loud. The body carries it. The open thing, which was not going to be decided today, is already being handled like a debt coming due.
The release you can do gets crowded out by the preparing. So put it down: the situation, as it stands, without a feeling word on the page, then read it back. Follow what is written — the next real step and nothing past that. The page holds it so you do not have to keep holding all of it. Steady practice does not need to be driven.

cells.tense: While the finished thing sat there waiting, the person was still standing at a doorway already behind them.
cells.act: lay the one step you can see, solidly
cells.ask: Lay the step you can actually see, at full strength — done, not planned. Nothing past it, no timetable on it.
cells.core:
The open room is here, and no one has stepped into it. The load that was finished got set down, and the person who set it down has not moved. Things stay undecided not because they are hard but because deciding has been left alone, and the whole business has started to feel like a waiting area.
Pushing at the stalled place will not bring it back. The hands will. So put one ordinary thing down at full weight — the step you can actually see, done solidly, no more of the plan demanded than that. Build small. A single plank set right carries the next one, and the next, and none of it needs deciding in the head first. The open stretch stops being somewhere you are stuck the moment one real foot lands on the ground.
cells.sheetLine: Everything's still undecided because the deciding was left alone.

cells.tense: Nobody watching would say the release is being kept by anyone, and the one doing it would likely agree.
cells.act: apprentice yourself to the material thing
cells.ask: Take something ordinary you already keep — a plant, a routine, a friendship — and study its rhythm rather than setting one. Expect nothing back from it.
cells.core:
Animals go quiet around this person at endings. Hard arrangements get dissolved without a scene, unspoken things get said gently, and hands that let go are invisible as hands. The loosening is real and continuous and it is unattributed. The one doing it would say, if asked, that there is nothing to attribute — things simply healed or did not.
So go back to the smallest version of it, the kind that leaves a fingerprint. Take one living thing — a plant, a routine, a friendship — and study how it moves through its days, keeping your own pace out of it. Fresh hands, ordinary care, no result demanded. That practice is smaller than everything already being done and it is the plainest form of the same thing, and it is the version where the one doing it becomes visible again. What has been let go of here is a skill someone could be named for.
cells.sheetLine: The loosening is real and no one — including you — is named for it.

cells.place: the open room before the choice, where anything can still become

attempts.check: The record says the seat is Potential itself — pure possibility before any choice — but a person's life can't literally be in that seat, so each cell reads it as the open, uncommitted thing in front of them. A reader could reasonably say the third cell puts a private history on them; no family, no door, no cause is written, only a stance they can disown. Each ask is small and independent of my read — tending, writing one line, laying one step, watching one thing — so it still teaches if I'm wrong. The sentence serving me more than them is the first cell's licence to release as if the difficulty had been meted out and answered; the cells are re-held so nothing prescribes.
